text:
priya: FYI — saw repeated GPU queue-depth spikes in eu-west around 06:12 UTC. Grafana panel shows saturation bursts on a few pods even though reserved pool capacity reports available GPUs. https://grafana.internal/d/redwood/capacity?orgId=1 :eyes:

mike: hmm, are these correlated with big batch jobs or autoscaler events?

priya: quick check: autoscaler only added 2 nodes later at 06:18 (ops-bot posted). spikes start ~06:10. batch_size histogram looks noisy.

katy: can you paste the PromQL you used?

priya: sure — the panel uses a rolling sum of queued requests per node + 95p latency:```
sum by(node) (queue_depth{region="eu-west"})
```

sam: two quick ideas: 1) probe flapping / kube-proxy conntrack exhaustion can make kubelet drop readiness briefly and route traffic weirdly, 2) large KV-cache misses cause huge first-token latencies which back up queues.

mike: +1 on checking node-level network conntrack. also check per-pod batch_size distribution (we saw a couple of clients send 512-token batches last week).

priya: added a temporary panel to correlate batch_size percentiles with queue_depth. query:```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_batch_size_bucket[5m])) by (le, pod))
```

ops-bot: autoscaler: scale_up group=eu-west-gpu from=48 to=50 reason="sustained_queue_depth" at=1765554298

katy: ops-bot says scale happened after the first spikes. so the autoscaler reaction was late for these bursts. can we tune the scaling signal to use a longer window or a different metric (e.g., sustained_queue_rate instead of instantaneous depth)?

sam: proposal: use a dual-signal alert for scale decisions: short-window rate (for immediate rapid scale) + sustained quantile of queue_depth over 5m to avoid chasing noise. also cap batch_size per-request via gateway to avoid single requests creating long blocking windows.

mike: also worth adding a low-cost guard: if queue_depth spike > 500 for <30s ignore for scaling, but for >2m trigger. current rule uses 1m for-for which is too sensitive.

priya: created PR for alert change:```
- alert: QueueDepthHigh
  expr: sum(queue_depth{region="eu-west"}) > 400
  for: 1m
+ alert: QueueDepthSustained
+ expr: sum_over_time(sum(queue_depth{region="eu-west"})[3m]) / 3 > 300
+ for: 2m
```

katy: can we also surface network drops / conntrack metrics on the capacity dashboard? add panel for conntrack_used and kubeproxy_errors.

priya: added conntrack panel and a small loglink widget to jump to the k8s events for affected nodes.

sam: quick retrospective: root cause likely combination of a handful of large-batch clients + short-lived probe variability. mitigation: 1) gateway batch-size limit, 2) dual-signal autoscaler, 3) give ops dashboard a batch_size vs queue depth correlation panel.

priya: marking this as "monitoring change in flight" — will follow up with an incident note if it recurs. :thumbsup:
